pages.title: Engineering & Design
pages.text: Home›The TowerDesign & EngineeringTHE TOWER DESIGN AND ENGINEERINGThe Structure Is The FormThis early engineering sketch reveals how the tower’s distinctive form was shaped through structure. The lines trace the changing geometry of the building as it rises, showing how architecture and engineering were developed together to turn a complex concept into a buildable structure Not a single office in the building faces south.A single formal act, subtracting a spiralling quadrant from a prismatic volume, created both the architectural identity and the structural system of Kuwait's most ambitious buildingTHE ENGINEERING FEATThe LamellaAt the foot of the tower, where the south wall begins its turn, the building opens into a lobby 24 metres high with not a single column standing in it. What holds it up is the lamella: a lattice of concrete members that gathers the weight of the tower above and carries it down to the ground around the edges of the spaceFive element types interlock to form the web, each shaped to the load it carries. pages.title: Sustainability
pages.text: Home›The TowerSustainabilityEnvironmental philosophyThe form is the strategyIn most buildings, sustainability arrives after the architecture is resolved, in the shape of solar panels, shading devices and green roofs. At Al Hamra Tower the environmental response generated the architecture. The spiralling form that makes the building unmistakable is the same act that removes the south facing glass, and the stone wall that defines the skyline is also the primary solar shieldSOM's structural engineers describe the process as symbiotic evolution. The structural system and the exterior form developed together, and neither could exist without the otherENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE01The Desert WallThe solid south wall, 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone, is the building's primary environmental strategy. Its geometry answers Kuwait's solar path directly. Openings are positioned according to the envelope's relationship to the sun at each floor level, so direct solar radiation never enters an officeZero south-facing offices, tower-wide02The Spiralling FormRemoving a quarter of each floor plate on the south side does two things at once. It opens Gulf views to every tenant and it reduces the total surface exposed to desert sun. SOM calls it a purely formal operation, with architecture and environmental engineering solved by the same geometric act30% less south facing surface than a conventional tower of equal area03Low E Insulating Glass55,000 square metres of curtain wall on the north, east and west facades use insulating glass with a low emissivity coating. Roughly 30% of the units are curved to wrap the tower's corners, with the bending and coating processes designed to work in tandem55,000 m² insulating curtain wall04Trencadis, Weight Reduced StoneThe upper floors of the limestone cladding use trencadis, a mesh coated with crushed limestone, in place of full tiles. It cuts facade weight substantially at height while holding the visual continuity of the monolithic stone wall. A material innovation driven by structural necessitySignificant weight reduction at height — same visual appearance05Smart Building InfrastructureA fibre optic backbone and an advanced building automation system, managed by a world leading facility management company, monitor and control every building system on every floor100% power supply redundancy across 5 substationsLeasing Inquiry→06Concrete Over SteelAl Hamra is one of the few reinforced concrete supertall buildings, a choice with long term sustainability implications. Concrete's thermal mass moderates internal temperature swings and its compressive strength allows efficient use of material. The 289 piles were designed for the chemistry of Kuwait's silty sand geology, to resist sulphate attack without corrosion195,000 m³ reinforced concrete — structural longevity by designThe solid south wall, and flared geometry, is generated in order to decrease the absorption of solar radiation. This wall not only protects the building from critical environmental conditions, it also assumes the role of structural backboneSkidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP — Structural Sustainability Statement

The upper floors of the limestone cladding use trencadis, a mesh coated with crushed limestone, in place of full tiles. It cuts facade weight substantially at height while holding the visual continuity of the monolithic stone wall. A material innovation driven by structural necessity
feature_cards.image_caption_en: Significant weight reduction at height, same visual appearance

feature_cards.body_en: The solid south wall, 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone, is the building's primary environmental strategy. Its geometry answers Kuwait's solar path directly. Openings are positioned according to the envelope's relationship to the sun at each floor level, so direct solar radiation never enters an office

timeline_entries.body_en: The lamella is built, a web of 24 metre curved elements arching outward from the core, cast in fiberglass formwork fabricated directly from 3D parametric models. It opens a column free lobby of 900 square metres. Engineers run non linear buckling analyses on every member before it carries load

A mixed use complex with a 200 metre tower is designed by Al Jazera Consultants. Excavation begins and 289 cast in place bored piles are sunk 22 to 27 metres into Kuwait's silty sand. Once the pour starts, the foundation work cannot stop

Kuwait City Municipality raises the maximum allowable building height to 400 metres. The client group engages Skidmore, Owings and Merrill to design a landmark. SOM begins concept design with the contractor already working below

SOM subtracts a spiralling quadrant from a prismatic volume and rotates it at every level above. Two hyperbolic paraboloid walls appear, the flared ribbons. The geometry turns the building transparent toward the Gulf and solid toward the desert. Construction begins
Al Hamra Tower tops out at 412.6 metres, among the ten tallest buildings in the world at completion. 258,000 square metres of Jura limestone stand finished in Sharq. Kuwait City has a new landmark

Al Hamra's environmental performance was not engineered into the building after the form was set. It was the form itself — every design decision that gave the tower its identity also solved an environmental problem.
SOM's structural engineers describe the process as symbiotic evolution. The structural system and the exterior form developed together, and neither could exist without the other
Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP — Structural Sustainability Statement

The solid south wall, and flared geometry, is generated in order to decrease the absorption of solar radiation. This wall not only protects the building from critical environmental conditions, it also assumes the role of structural backbone

The Al Hamra Tower's geometry was generated by a single decisive act: subtracting a spiraling quadrant from a simple prismatic volume, then rotating it incrementally at each higher level. The result is two hyperbolic paraboloid walls — the iconic flared ribbons — that extend the full 412 metres of the building's height.
